title: Streamline GPU node state machine and upgrade k8s client libraries
creator: Priya Narang
description: Refactor the GPU node lifecycle/state-machine and move to supported k8s client libraries to reduce flakiness, simplify code paths, and improve autoscaler performance. Current motivation: duplicated transition logic across node controller and pool manager causes inconsistent state (Draining vs Preempted), memory churn during large-scale reconciles, and brittle heuristics that surface as autoscaler instability under bursty traffic. Scope: (1) consolidate state transition code into a single state-machine module with clear invariants, (2) upgrade client-go and controller-runtime to the tested versions used by our cloud provider images, (3) remove legacy feature flags and dead code paths, (4) add deterministic unit/integration tests and a small e2e that simulates node preemption and node replacement. Acceptance criteria listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated node state-machine implemented and used by gpu-pool-manager and autoscaler components
Client-go and controller-runtime upgraded to versions that match cluster control plane; no API breakages in staging
Unit tests covering all state transitions (Provisioning, Ready, Draining, Terminating, Preempted) with >90% coverage for state-machine module
Integration test in staging shows reduced reconciliation CPU by >=15% and median node replacement latency improved by >=200ms
No regression in existing rollout canary for a 24h period; automatic rollback hooks pass
comments: 2026-02-18 - Triage: Identified three hotspots: duplicated TransitionToDraining(), excessive list/watch churn, and out-of-sync node annotations. Marking as tech-debt P1 due to recent mini-incidents in us-west-2.

2026-02-22 - Spike results: benchmarked current reconcile loop on a 2000-node sim cluster. Observed 12% CPU overhead attributable to repeated annotation writes and ~250ms median latency per reconcile iteration during scale events.

2026-02-27 - Design decision: move to a single state-machine abstraction (state_machine.NodeState) and introduce explicit immutable events for transitions. Trade-off: initial larger PR surface area vs long-term reduced cognitive load and fewer accidental transitions.

2026-03-01 - Dependency decision: upgrade client-go to v0.29.8 and controller-runtime to 0.14.x to match provider SDK. Risk: requires small adaptation for some Watch semantics; mitigations included compatibility wrappers in state-machine adapter.
2026-03-03 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4821 — includes core state-machine, adapters, and initial unit tests. Marked WIP; not yet wired into autoscaler loop.

2026-03-05 - Code review notes from @Maya Singh: please add metrics for transition counts and time spent in each state; consider exponential backoff when annotation write conflicts occur. Action: added metrics meters and conflict backoff with jitter.

2026-03-08 - Integration test: staging run failing intermittently due to race between node_replace controller and node-annotation reconciler. Root cause: both used direct writes instead of compare-and-swap. Fix: centralize writes through state-machine writer with optimistic locking.

2026-03-10 - Re-run staging: stability improved. Observed 18% CPU reduction in reconcile loop and median replacement latency down by ~230ms. Leaving remaining work: finalize rollout plan, add e2e for preemption scenario, update upgrade notes for SRE.
2026-03-10 - Blocker-ish: Need security review on upgraded dependencies for CVE check. Created follow-up to run SBOM and dependency scanning prior to production rollout.
